comparison_note: 7/13 = 53.8% on this sub-cohort. This is a like-for-like comparison ONLY against that sub-cohort and must not be quoted as a benchmark score. Frontier on the full 328: o1 51.2%, agent 55.5%, RAG 59.4%.
consequence_for_plan: the next unit is not a bigger space. It is: make the FEATURE SET the thing that is discovered rather than chosen, and persist the weights in the external store so they survive across sessions and environments. Four hand-chosen features with learned weights transferred; the loop now has a signal strong enough to learn from.
features: coverage: fraction of the name's own words present in the problem text
doc_overlap: fraction of the problem's words present in the artifact's docstring
stub_hit: does the name share a word with the stub's own name
depth: small penalty for dotted depth

followup_one_feature_test.consequence: feature DISCOVERY is not the win. Training-only forward selection scored by rank reduced eight features to one and lost two items. A discovery loop must be scored by EXECUTED SOLVES on the training half, which is more expensive and has not been done.
lessons: the top-10 metric is NOT the outcome: one feature matched on rank and lost two items on execution (shallow wrong names beat ntheory.primetest.is_square and functions.primepi)
the extra features are load-bearing but weak: depth and docstring overlap bought is_square and primepi
defensible claim is 7/13 with the fitted four-feature ranking; one-feature gets 5/13; both held-out, neither a benchmark score
followup_one_feature_test.method: forward selection using ONLY the training half; the test half was never inspected during selection
followup_one_feature_test.question: can the four-feature combination be reduced (Elon's law: remove before adding)?

limits: one benchmark family: same 26 sympy items from the same benchmark; NOT run on networkx or the other 24 libraries
6/13 held-out still fail: todok (rank inf), partition (157), isprime (86), primeomega (79), flat (40), use (3 but wrong body shape)
weights are fitted on oracle outcomes -- legal (no model, no stored world facts) but supervised by the benchmark's own tests; an unseen environment must supply the feedback signal
the two splits chose DIFFERENT weights ([2,2,0,1] vs [0,6,3,1]) and both transferred: the feature set is right, the exact weights are sufficient not identified
the four features were chosen BY HAND; only their weights were learned

missed_signal.finding: 17 of 26 required names contain a word literally present in the problem text
missed_signal.why_the_docstring_ranker_missed_it: a long docstring sharing common words outscored an exact name match; conversely exact-name alone fails on jacobi_symbol (rank 44) because 'symbol' is noise. The signals are complementary.

false: that the ranking problem is closed: 6/13 held-out still fail with the known failure class
true: a ranking fitted on 13 items solves 7 of 13 held-out items through the benchmark's own hidden tests; both splits reproduce (7/13, 8/13)
the learned object is four weights over four computed features: no table, no model, no stored facts
beats every fixed rule in the previous four receipts (3/40 -> 7/32 -> 8/32 -> 7/13 held-out)
unproven: transfer to other libraries, the full 328-item benchmark, and unseen environments
whether the four features are the right four; they were hand-chosen and only weights learned

what_is_learned: FOUR WEIGHTS OVER FOUR COMPUTED FEATURES -- a statement about how this family of artifacts names things. Not a list of names. Computed, four floats, fitted in seconds, applied to 13 unseen items in both directions, externalisable as JSON without retraining.
why_different: the previous four fitted nothing and measured on the same items they scored. This fits on half the items and measures on the other half.
